overview: This bill, the Acquisition Reform and Cost Assessment Act, reorganizes how the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) buys goods, services, and technology. It creates an Assistant Secretary for Acquisition who would serve as the VA's chief buying officer and oversee a new Office of Acquisition, with all purchasing, contracting, logistics, and supply chain work across the VA's health, benefits, and cemetery branches consolidated under that office within a year. Large projects, defined as those expected to cost more than $1 billion over their life or $200 million a year, would each get a certified program manager, would be checked by independent outside reviewers, and would receive independent cost estimates from a new Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation who reports to the VA Secretary and to Congress. The bill also calls for at least doubling the VA's acquisition internship programs to build its purchasing workforce. The Senate passed it on December 11, 2025, and as of December 15, 2025, it was awaiting action in the House.
for: Supporters say the VA has struggled with costly, delayed technology and supply projects, and that clear lines of responsibility, independent cost checks, and trained managers will help protect taxpayer money and veterans' care.
against: Critics say a major reorganization adds new layers of officials and outside contractors, and that moving purchasing away from the health and benefits branches could slow decisions for the people closest to veterans' needs.
